cloudflare.name: Cloudflare
cloudflare.description: Unfiltered public resolver with encrypted DNS support and a documented privacy commitment
features: Limited public-resolver transaction/debug logs are deleted within 25 hours
Source IP addresses are truncated and the truncated value is deleted within 25 hours
Privacy commitments are covered by a published independent accounting-firm audit
Separate malware and family-filtering resolver variants exist but are not selected here
cloudflare.jurisdiction: United States; service behavior is governed by Cloudflare's published public-resolver privacy commitment
cloudflare.best_for: An unfiltered public resolver with independently audited privacy commitments

quad9.name: Quad9
quad9.description: Non-profit DNS with Swiss privacy and threat blocking
features: Does not retain information that can identify an individual user under normal service conditions
Shares limited non-identifying counters for malicious-domain queries only with the threat-intelligence analyst that contributed that domain
Threat blocking combines many public and commercial intelligence sources
quad9.jurisdiction: Switzerland (Zuerich); operated by the Swiss Quad9 Foundation
quad9.best_for: Threat-domain blocking without retaining client IPs in ordinary query logs

adguard.name: AdGuard DNS
adguard.description: EU-based DNS with comprehensive ad and tracker blocking
features: Default public endpoints also block domains classified as malicious
Public DNS policy describes aggregated performance metrics and no user-specific collection beyond what service operation requires
Stores an anonymous database of requested domains from the last 24 hours
adguard.jurisdiction: Cyprus (Limassol); ADGUARD SOFTWARE LIMITED is the data controller
adguard.best_for: Public DNS-level ad, tracker, and malicious-domain filtering

notes.dnssec: All providers perform server-side DNSSEC validation. No client-side NRPT configuration required.
notes.doh: For the managed endpoints, Windows DNS Client uses DNS over HTTPS. Classic-DNS fallback is disabled in REQUIRE mode and permitted in ALLOW mode; applications with an independent resolver stack are outside this policy.
notes.ipv6: Effective IPv6 resolvers are configured alongside IPv4 only when the adapter binding and global IPv6 transport are enabled. On a binding-enabled adapter whose transport is intentionally disabled with DisabledComponents=0xFF, schema-5 BAVR separately manages the persisted native IPv6 resolver/DoH state used by Windows Settings without claiming active IPv6 traffic.
